A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOP research, with matching authors, core method, and retained experiments. All pages, equations, tables, and figures were readable. v1 has no appendices; v2's Appendices A and B were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining and benchmark results for 340M, 1.8B, and 7B models in Table 2, plus a 16M-model training-loss experiment in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds DS-MTP comparisons, math/code evaluations, star-graph experiments, speculative-decoding measurements, sensitivity studies, and appendix training curves.

M1.justification: The core TOP target construction, auxiliary head, and default loss remain unchanged. Sections 5.4–5.5 add limited procedural extensions: speculative decoding using ordered TOP predictions validated by the NTP head, and unequal NTP/TOP loss-weight variants.

E1.justification: v2 retains FineWeb-Edu and the eight original benchmarks, adds MMLU, and introduces continued training on Stack-Edu Python and OpenMathInstruct-2 with HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH evaluation. It also adds synthetic star-graph pathfinding and decoding tests on wiki, books, code, and math texts.

E2.justification: DS-MTP changes from a cited, planned comparison in v1 to an evaluated baseline alongside NTP/MTP/TOP at all three sizes in Table 2. v2 also evaluates two- and four-head MTP and DS-MTP variants in the star-graph comparison, substantially extending comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Retained base-pretraining settings agree, while new experiments introduce continued-training budgets, few-shot math/code protocols, pass@16/32/64, graph train/test splits and different layer-matching controls, 5,000-snippet decoding evaluations, and configuration sweeps. The newly stated zero-shot setting for existing benchmarks documents their protocol without establishing a change to those evaluations.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's MTP-head loss illustration, v2 adds a TOP-versus-MTP loss comparison, tests lookahead across graph structures and head counts, and studies window size and loss weighting in Tables 7–8. Appendix B adds componentwise training trajectories used to examine behavior such as DS-MTP's weak downstream performance.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional loss trajectories are not identified as uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Shared NTP/MTP/TOP scores on the original eight benchmarks are unchanged. v2 adds extensive results in Tables 2–8 and Appendix B, including TOP's 100% accuracy on G(5,5) versus the best baseline's 19.5%. Generative results are mixed: for example, 7B TOP scores 20.40% on MATH versus NTP's 21.74%. These are new comparisons, not improvements to the original scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal DS-MTP definitions in Equations 5–8 and a limited FLOP/parameter derivation in Section 4.2 and Table 1, replacing qualitative overhead discussion with explicit expressions. The central TOP mathematics remains unchanged, and no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1's principal empirical claim concerns eight standard NLP benchmarks against NTP and MTP. v2 broadens its abstract, contributions, and conclusion to DS-MTP, nine benchmarks, math/code generation, and solving the hardest tested star graph where the comparators fail. The conclusion also acknowledges weaker speculative decoding.

C2.justification: v1's tentative interpretation of TOP as a regularizer is removed. v2 adds interpretations concerning DS-MTP overfitting, task-dependent lookahead windows, and stronger learning signals from higher TOP weighting. It also discusses decoding limitations and explicitly limits extrapolation to larger models and longer training.

D1.justification: v2 adds configuration provenance, continued-training hyperparameters in Table 10, detailed synthetic-experiment settings, and disclosure of two weeks per 7B model on eight H200 GPUs. The original configuration table largely moves to Appendix A, but its device-batch-size and gradient-accumulation rows are omitted. The code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial Related Work section covering masked and denoising objectives, retrieval-based training, and newer MTP approaches, including register tokens and continuous reasoning. New benchmark, dataset, and configuration-source citations further broaden the positioning beyond v1's concentrated NTP/MTP and learning-to-rank discussion.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the introduction/background discussion, expands the explanation of Algorithm 1, subdivides the method and experiments, and moves training configurations into Appendix A. The early-preprint Future Additions ending is replaced by dedicated Related Work and Limitations sections and an expanded conclusion, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 becomes a two-panel comparison, and Table 2 is transposed and replaces colored differences with bold best scores. Numerous new experimental tables, graph illustrations, and appendix loss plots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important gaps in v1: DS-MTP comparison, generative evaluation, and direct star-graph testing of the lookahead motivation were previously only planned. These experiments, sensitivity studies, and disclosed decoding failures substantially strengthen the evidence and clarify applicability. Mixed generative gains, unexplained DS-MTP weakness, and absent uncertainty reporting warrant caution about broad claims, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
